title: Regulated Accounts Messaging Experiments - pilots & competitive notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Short experiment guide for messaging to regulated accounts (fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense).
- Capture initial hypotheses, competitive counterpoints, pilot metrics, and quick rebut scripts for sales/solutions.
- This is intentionally lightweight and iterative: use for sprint-level messaging tests with SDRs, AMs, and solutions engineers.

Summary hypothesis (what we want to test):
- Regulated buyers care most about predictable inference economics + auditable controls. If we lead with predictable unit cost, clear migration paths (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and auditability for model outputs, we will convert small pilots into committed contracts more often than generic capability-led messaging.

Overarching narrative we want to validate:
- "Bring production-grade LLM inference to regulated workloads without sacrificing auditability, cost predictability, or developer velocity."
- Evidence to validate: SLA language, pilot cost model, short audit trails for prompts/outputs, and a clear fallback story for outages and model regressions.

Industry-specific framing, quick scripts, and metrics to collect:

1) Fintech - payments, lending, fraud detection
- Key persona: platform engineering lead; Head of ML; security/compliance officer
- Primary pain: model unpredictability drives cost overruns and regulatory risk (KYC, AML audits)
- Core message: deterministic inference economics + explainable audit trails for decisioning models
- 1-liner sales script: "Reduce per-decision variance and get audit-ready inference: predictable token economics, rollouts with canaries, and tamper-evident logs for every request."
- Proof points to bring: documented pilot cost runbook, sample audit export, latency SLOs for decisioning windows, references or anonymized case study numbers
- Pilot success metrics: cost per decision within 15% of estimate; audit export completeness; latency P95 < 200ms for production path
- Common objections and quick rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We need absolute explainability for credit decisions" -> Rebuttal: "We support structured outputs and deterministic pipelines; combine model outputs with rule-based checkpoints and produce exportable decision artifacts."
  - Objection: "Vendor lock and model change control" -> Rebuttal: "Versioned model pinning plus canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variants reduces risk."
- Collateral suggestions: one-pager titled 'Inference Controls for Financial Decisioning' and a cost-sensitivity worksheet

2) Healthcare - clinical assistants, coding/billing, patient triage
- Key persona: clinical informatics lead; security/compliance; procurement
- Primary pain: PHI security, provenance of clinical suggestions, validation workflow integration
- Core message: private deployment options with KMS integration and verifiable provenance for model outputs, plus developer ergonomics so clinicians can iterate safely
- 1-liner sales script: "Run models in a VPC or on-prem with KMS-backed keys, evidence trails for outputs, and configurable human-in-the-loop gates for clinical workflows."
- Proof points: architecture diagram for private deployment, KMS integration notes, red-team summary, sample HITL flow for triage
- Pilot success metrics: zero cross-tenant data leakage, compliance checklist signoff, clinician acceptance rate in controlled trial > 70%
- Common objections and rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We need full on-prem air-gapped deployment" -> Rebuttal: "We support a private control plane + optional air-gap packages; propose a phased approach starting with VPC and running a small on-prem exchange."
  - Objection: "How do we prove model outputs haven't been tampered with?" -> Rebuttal: "We surface tamper-evident logs and signed export bundles tied to KMS keys for each run."
- Collateral: architecture reference, short compliance checklist, sample patient-safety gate flow

3) Legal - contract review, research, e-discovery
- Key persona: Head of Legal Ops; CISO; SME attorneys
- Primary pain: confidentiality of documents; reproducible transformations; defensible redactions and audit trails
- Core message: private model hosting with per-request provenance and deterministic transformation logs for legal defensibility
- 1-liner: "Keep sensitive corpora inside your network while using modern LLMs that record why and how outputs were produced."
- Proof points: demo of redaction controls, exportable provenance logs, sample NDAs for pilot scope
- Pilot success metrics: successful redaction tests, reproducibility of 80% of key extraction results, acceptance by legal ops
- Objections + rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We can just use existing text-extraction vendors" -> Rebuttal: "Those vendors often force data egress; we provide private deployments and audit logs so you keep custody while improving accuracy through custom prompts and evals."
- Collateral: short demo script for e-discovery, checklist for evidence collection

4) Enterprise SaaS - product teams adding smart features
- Key persona: CTO/VP Product; platform engineers; lead customer success manager
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency and cost at scale; operational burden of model rollouts across customers
- Core message: same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private so you can build once and choose the deployment that matches customers without rewrite
- 1-liner: "Ship conversational features fast, then dial in economics and isolation as customers scale."
- Proof points: migration story, SDK examples, performance dashboards for token-level cost breakdowns
- Pilot metrics: time-to-integrate < 2 weeks, first 100k tokens cost within budget, per-route latency SLO met
- Objections + rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We will outgrow hosted and need custom infra" -> Rebuttal: "We provide reserved capacity and private deployment patterns with the same API so client code doesn't change."
- Collateral: migration checklist, code snippets, troubleshooting runbook for rollout

5) Gov / Defense - regulated contractors and civilian agencies
- Key persona: program manager; security accreditation officer; integrator partner
- Primary pain: IL5/IL6 type requirements, supply-chain attestations, long procurement cycles, limited cloud regions
- Core message: tailored private deployment options, supply chain transparency, and hardened operational practices to meet accreditation needs while supporting developer integration patterns
- 1-liner: "Committed deployment modalities and audit chains for mission-critical inference with procurement-friendly SLAs."
- Proof points: third-party audits, SOC-like artifacts, hardened deployment checklist, examples of limited-region options
- Pilot metrics: accreditation artifacts delivered; red-team findings remediated within agreed SLA; demo in restricted-region environment
- Objections + rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We need to see extensive compliance paperwork first" -> Rebuttal: "Provide a minimal compliance pack to start discovery; parallel path for audit delivery during pilot."
- Collateral: executive summary for contracting, hardened deployment runbook

Competitive analysis notes (high level):
- Cloud AI endpoints (big public clouds): strength = procurement familiarity and ecosystem; weakness = opaque unit economics at token scale and limited offline/private patterns across vendors.
- LLM API pure-plays: strength = simplicity and model access; weakness = limited enterprise SLAs, variable predictability, sometimes lacks private deployment options.
- Inference infra vendors / OSS stacks: strength = control and cost-optimization potential; weakness = high operational burden, slower time-to-value for product teams.

Where Redwood can position to win these accounts:
- Differentiator 1: unified API across deployment modes - reduces integration friction during procurement and migration.
- Differentiator 2: cost transparency tools - token-level breakdowns and pilot runbooks that forecast economics under real workloads.
- Differentiator 3: auditability - KMS integration, signed logs, and exportable evidence for compliance reviews.
- Differentiator 4: graceful fallbacks - model variant routing and automatic fallback reduces operational risk in mission-critical flows.

Competitive risk areas to avoid promising prematurely:
- Deep claims about 'universal explainability' - better to promise structured outputs and reproducible artifacts rather than full black-box explanations.
- Guarantees about model parity vs top LLM providers on open benchmarks - focus on end-to-end product metrics instead (latency, cost, quality per task).

Experiment plan for the next 90 days:
- Week 0-2: create three tailored one-pagers (fintech, healthcare, gov) and two technical deep-dive decks for SEs.
- Week 2-6: run messaging A/B tests with SDR/AM outreach sequences and track response rates by claim (cost predictability vs auditability vs migration ease).
- Week 6-12: run two pilot offers: a 4-week fintech pilot and a 6-week healthcare pilot with defined acceptance criteria (metrics above). Collect quantitative metrics and qualitative feedback.
- Week 12+: iterate collateral based on pilot learnings and prepare a go/no-go for an enterprise motion template.

Sales enablement quick wins:
- Provide SEs with two-sentence rebut scripts and a 1-page pilot cost model template they can adapt live in calls.
- Pre-bake compliance starter pack for pilots (what artifact we will deliver and when).
- Build a short demo that shows token-level cost breakdown and an export of tamper-evident logs in <5 min.

Open questions / data to collect in pilots:
- Typical token distribution and sequence length for decisioning models in fintech customers.
- Acceptance threshold for human-in-the-loop gating in clinical flows.
- Procurement blockers in gov contracts that delay pilots beyond usefulness.

Appendix - suggested artifacts to include with pilot:
- Pilot cost runbook (spreadsheet) with model/quantization/batching knobs and example cost scenarios
- Minimal compliance pack: architecture diagrams, KMS notes, SOC-like summary, proof-of-concept signed logs
- SE demo scripts for common objections and short video clips for self-serve assets

Notes to team:
- This is a working doc; please append pilot outcomes and any direct customer quotes to the linked confluence page (confluence:GTMP-1223).
- Keep language conservative on explainability and accuracy guarantees. Focus on operational controls, evidence, and measurable pilot success metrics.
